###chapter 1
"Stop! Please, just stop!" I kept begging, but they didn't give a shit. I kicked and squirmed. Nothing. "I'm your freaking Luna!" I screamed until my throat burned. Then, a laugh echoed from the next room. His laugh. It instantly crushed my spirit. "Rhys, please..." I croaked out, completely spent.

"Get the kid out, then kill it. Dump her in the woods. Let her rot or survive on her own. I don't care."

No way. He couldn't say that. It was our kid. "Our baby," I whispered.

"That thing is a mistake from the Moon Goddess. And I'm fixing it." His cold voice drifted in. Coward wouldn't even look me in the eye. "Cut her. Now. That's an order."

"Yes, Alpha." 

God, coming here was a massive mistake. Giving him my whole damn life? Even bigger mistake.

"Oh, hey, doc?" A sweet, sickening voice chimed in from the hallway. Blair. My stepsister. I clenched my jaw so hard it hurt. "Skip the pain meds. Make sure she feels every single cut."

"Understood, Luna." The doctor looked at me, his eyes full of pity. But the second he grabbed the blade, I knew I was dead meat.

*I'm so sorry, sweetie. Mommy can't protect you. I wanted you so bad.* I tried to reach down to touch my belly, but the nurses had me pinned tight with leather straps. As the doctor stepped up, the metal caught the light. Silver.

"Is that... silver?" I barely breathed the word. He gave a grim nod. That was it. Blair didn't just want my title; she wanted me in a grave. She'd cooked up those fake photos, lied about me sleeping around, and he bought it. I hadn't touched another man. And after this? I never damn well would.

Why, Goddess? Why pair me with this monster just to rip my baby away? My poor little pup.

Tears streamed down my face as the cold metal sliced my stomach open. Inside, my baby kicked wildly. He knew. He knew it was too damn early. This was a straight-up execution for both of us.

"Bring me the dead pup."

"Right away, Alpha." The pain was blinding. Every slice tore through my nerves until I couldn't hold it in anymore. I shrieked. Warm blood rushed down my flanks, dripping onto the cold floor. *Drip. Drip.* I fought the straps, but the silver was already draining my strength.

*Forgive me, baby.* 

They were letting me bleed out. I knew it was coming, but it still hurt like hell. I used to worship my mate. But watching them tear my baby out of my own flesh? That love died right then and there.

"Please... just let me hold him. Once." I strained against the cuffs, reaching out. The doctor, tears spilling down his cheeks, actually showed some mercy. He gently placed my baby on my chest.

He was absolutely gorgeous. I nuzzled his tiny face, mixing our scents together. He was my soul. My missing half. Forever.

"Doc, wrap it up. Now."

"Yes, Alpha." The doctor snatched my baby away and bolted, leaving me sliced open and freezing on the table.

My vision started to fade. Then the door clicked. In walked Blair, wearing that disgusting, victorious smirk.

"Told you I'd steal your life, Lyra. Told you I'd take your man. And oh, I have. We've been busy ever since he found out you're a 'cheater'." Blair leaned down and kissed my cheek. I growled, baring my teeth. "He's amazing in bed. Don't worry, though. I'll pop out another son for him." She patted her flat stomach. I burst out laughing. "What the hell are you laughing at?" she snapped.

"I can smell the beta all over you, sis. That's Gareth's kid. And guess what? It's a girl. Nice try, loser."

She hissed, her claws sliding out to slit my throat. But the door literally flew off its hinges. In walked my mate—the man I now loathed with every fiber of my being. His eyes were blood-red. I laughed even harder.

"You lying bitch!" he roared. He backhanded Blair so hard she flew across the room.

"Damon!" Blair shrieked, slamming into the wall. "What are you doing?!" She scrambled to her feet. I felt more blood gush out of my stomach. I let my eyelids flutter shut.

"You lied to me!" he bellowed. His Alpha aura flared, rattling the walls, but I was too numb to care. The silver poison was already creeping up my veins, heading straight for my dying heart. "That was my baby! I smell my own scent on him! He was mine!" Damon's eyes burned red, tears welling up. "You told me she slept around! You said it wasn't mine!"

"She did cheat! Okay? I guess... I guess I got the baby part wrong."

"You told me you smelled another wolf!" He lunged at her again. The last thing I saw before my eyes gave out was him holding our dead baby. God, I hated that sight. He did this to us. Not Blair. Him.

Sure, she played her cards right, but he's the one who didn't trust me. He couldn't even wait a few damn days to check the pup's scent. This was on him. He ruined all of us.

*Goddess, please just let me die. I'm done. Take me to my baby.*

"Save her!"

"No way!" Blair shrieked. "I'm the Luna now! You marked me last night!" Ah. So that explained the sudden, agonizing pain I felt yesterday. The sheer disgust made bile rise in my throat. "I'm carrying your kid!" she lied.

I chuckled again, a bloody sound. I forced my eyes open. Damon was hovering over me, looking panicked. "Lyra, stay with me. Don't you dare close your eyes."

"It's... the beta's... kid," I wheezed, laughing as pure horror washed over his face. "She's screwing... the beta." I grinned, spitting blood right onto his face.

"Fix her!"

"Hell no!" I snapped, unleashing every drop of my remaining power. "Freeze." I pushed my own Alpha command into the room, locking everyone—including my mate—dead in their tracks.

"How...?" Damon stared down at me, begging with his eyes. "Please, Lyra. Let me save you."

"I carry the blood of the Moon Goddess herself, you idiot. You don't get to save me. You didn't deserve our baby, and you sure as hell don't deserve me. You were weak. Now? You've got nothing." I smiled right at his stupid, crying face as my soul slipped away. 

And just like that, I was out.

###chapter 2
My eyes snapped open. Holy crap, I was breathing.

"Lyra! Get a move on, you're gonna be late!"

I bolted upright, head spinning. What the hell? Where was I?

"Lyra!"

The voice yelled again. I shook off the daze, slid out of bed, and scanned the room. Wait. No way. This was my old bedroom from back in the day.

I hadn't set foot in this place since the day I got matched with Damon, my so-called mate. 

*Knock, knock.*

The door swung open. It was Mom. My brain short-circuited. I didn't even think—I just lunged forward and threw my arms around her. 

"Mom! Oh my god, you're actually here!" I burst into tears, sobbing into her shoulder. "I missed you so damn much."

"Whoa, Lyra. Easy, girl." She chuckled, giving my back a gentle pat. "I literally saw you yesterday." She pulled back, her warm amber eyes—the exact same shade as mine—staring into my face. "Happy birthday, sweetie."

I leaned my face into her hands. Then, it hit me. Today was my last day in this house. I was turning eighteen. The day I met my mate.

"Thanks, Mom," I mumbled.

"Fingers crossed you find your mate today and start your real life," she said, beaming.

My stomach did a violent flip. Cold sweat broke out. Hell no. I didn't want to meet Damon. Not after the horror show I'd already lived through.

"Honestly? I'd rather just stay right here with you," I said, forcing a smile and planting a quick kiss on her cheek. "I don't wanna leave you and Ronnie behind."

But inside, my mind was racing. Damon. That bastard thought I cheated. He murdered my baby, then he murdered me. And Mom? He slaughtered her too, claiming she helped me cheat. Ronnie—Blair’s dad and Mom's husband—just stood there and watched her bleed out. Sure, the guy loved my mom, but he was a spineless coward. His snake of a daughter, Blair, was the puppet master behind the whole damn thing, and he didn't do a single thing to stop her.

I got why he backed his own kid, but I hated him for it. Both of them could rot in hell.

"Oh, baby. You won't miss us," Mom said, kissing my cheek. "We’re gonna be right there with you, every single step."

I squeezed her hand tight. 

"Mom, seriously. Can we just pack up and go? Just you and me. Let's dump Ronnie and Blair and head back to Dad's pack."

My dad, the Silvermoon Alpha, was a crappy husband, but he wasn't a bad guy. Yeah, he got wasted and cheated on Mom. He swore up and down it was a setup by some rival Alpha to tear them apart, but Mom said it didn't change a thing. The damage was done. 

That betrayal had caused her to miscarry my baby brother. She just couldn't get past the pain.

"No, sweetie. I can't go back there." Mom’s smile vanished, and she looked away, her shoulders slumping.

"I don't want to get stabbed in the back, Mom. Not like you did. I don't want a mate. Period." I let the words slip out, cold and honest.

"Mates don't hurt each other, baby," she tried to reassure me, but her smile was shaky.

I shuddered. Oh, Mom. You have no idea what mates are capable of.

"Would you hate me if I rejected him?" I asked.

"God, no, sweetie. The Moon Goddess lays out the path, sure, but we're the ones who walk it. If he's a jerk, reject his ass."

"What if he's the Alpha's son?"

Mom froze, her eyes locking onto mine. She knew the drill. If it was the Alpha's kid, I was trapped. They'd never let me walk. An Alpha needs to claim his true mate—even if it's just for twenty-four hours—to unlock his full power. 

"Lyra... what do you know?" she whispered, searching my face.

I grabbed her arm and dragged her deeper into the room, away from the door. "I don't know anything for sure. But I'm terrified. If I end up with Blair's boyfriend, I'm a dead woman walking. Mom, think about it. The odds of him matching with some high-ranking Alpha girl are way higher than him getting stuck with a Beta's daughter." I shook my head. "I want out."

She went quiet, processing the math. I could see the realization hit her. "Okay, baby. But running away is out. It'll look way too suspicious. You'll just have to mask your scent whenever he's around."

I threw my hands up. "And how the hell am I supposed to do that?"

"There are things from my past I wanted to leave buried... but if you're dead set on this..." She paused, waiting. I nodded hard. "Fine. Let me make some calls. You're staying home from school today."

I threw my arms around her neck again. "Thank you, Mom. Seriously. I'd be lost without you."

"I love you, baby. I'm always in your corner. Promise." She kissed my cheek and slipped out, closing the door.

The second she was gone, I grabbed my phone. I stared at the screen, checking the date. 2018. Holy shit. I was six years in the past. Six years before the nightmare. Today was the exact day I met Damon. This was my do-over. I could fix everything. I could survive. And this time, my baby would live.

I pressed my hand against my flat stomach. "Hang tight, little one. This time, nobody touches you."

I stripped, ran into the bathroom, and hopped in the shower. No way was I facing this new life looking like a hot mess. Afterward, wrapped in a towel, I stood in my closet trying to pick an outfit. 

Then, I heard the bedroom door creak open.

I was about to call out to Mom, but the footsteps were too light, too sneaky. Not Mom. I slipped behind my heavy winter coats and held my breath.

"I'm telling you, if she's Damon's mate, I'll slit her throat."

"Are you crazy, Shan?" Terra's whiny voice came through the phone speaker.

"I'm dead serious. Damon is mine."

"Yeah, only because you threw yourself at him. He was totally hoping Blair would notice him."

"Shut your damn mouth, Terra!" Blair hissed, her eyes probably flashing. "He belongs to me."

"Whatever, I gotta go. Get your ass moving before I leave you behind," Terra snapped, and the line went dead.

A car horn honked outside. Blair reached out to grab something from my shelf, but I lunged and snatched her wrist.

"What the hell do you think you're doing in my closet?"

"Lyra?!" Blair gasped, her jaw dropping.

I squeezed. Hard. *Crack.*

She started to scream, but I slapped my hand over her mouth, muffling the noise.

"You're lucky I only snapped one finger, bitch. You just threatened to murder me. Did you forget who you're talking to? A Beta's kid threatening an Alpha's daughter?" I scoffed.

"I didn't say shit!" she snarled, her bones already knitting back together.

"Lie to me again and I'll break every single bone in your hand and hold them in place while they heal crooked." I grinned, watching her start to shake. "Now. Did you threaten me?"

"Yes!" she shrieked. "Because you're gonna steal Damon!"

"I don't want your pathetic little boyfriend. Keep him. He's trash." I shoved her back. "Now get the hell out of my room before I decide to actually break something else."

I turned my back on her, grabbing a pair of low-rise jeans and a tank top.

"What the fuck is your problem?!" she spat.

"You. Get out." I let my wolf push to the surface, my eyes flashing. I slammed her with an Alpha command, forcing her body to move. She stumbled backward, out of my room. 

Stupid bitch. Sneaking into my space to steal my stuff? My wolf growled deep in my chest. *Our territory.*

I took a breath, calmed down, and locked the door. I hopped back onto the bed and grabbed my phone. I needed to map out every single detail of the next six years. Damon and Blair had no idea what was coming. They were going to pay. Every. Single. Cent.

###chapter 3
"Start packing, Lyra." Mom barged in, cutting right through my brainstorming. 

I blinked up from my notebook. "Wait, what? Why?"

"You're crashing at your dad's for the summer. The Alpha already cleared it." Mom beamed, tapping my shoulder. "Move it, kiddo. Get your stuff together."

I scrambled up and bolted over to her. "Seriously? I'm free?"

"Only till fall, sweetie. Then you're back. Had to sign my life away to promise you'd return."

My face fell. "Ugh, Mom, this place sucks. I hate it here." Honestly, I wanted payback, but keeping my distance from *him* came first. 

"Trust me, baby. It'll make sense when you see your dad." She smoothed my hair, planted a quick kiss on my cheek, and nudged me. "Chop chop."

"Fine, fine." I kissed her cheek, and she slipped out. 

I swiped my phone, locked the screen, and spun toward the closet. I threw clothes into my duffel, then made a move for the bathroom. Right then, the front door downstairs slammed so hard the walls shook. 

"I freaking knew it!" Blair's screech echoed through the floorboards. 

Whatever. I ignored the drama, swept my toiletries off the counter, grabbed my laptop and chargers, and shoved them into my pack. Time to go.

"Blair, what is your problem?" Ronnie sat at the kitchen table, nursing his coffee, while Mom bustled around. 

I rolled my suitcase into the kitchen just as Blair burst in, throwing herself into her dad's arms. "Daddy, I'm not Damon's mate!"

"Whoa, how do you know that?" Ronnie hugged her tight. 

I couldn't help it—I snorted. 

Blair's head whipped toward me, eyes blazing. She lunged. "It's you! You trashy little bitch!" Her claws aimed straight for my face. 

I didn't even blink. I just swung my hand and backhanded her ass across the room.

"Lyra!" Ronnie roared, jumping up. 

Mom clicked her tongue. "Oh, shut it, Ronnie. Don't yell at her for self-defense. Blair swung first." Mom set a plate of breakfast on the table. "Sit down and eat, Lyra. Big day ahead."

Ronnie blinked. "Wait, babe? Why is she packed?"

"She's heading to her dad's for the summer." Mom turned to me, arms wide. "Come on, sweetie. Eat up. Your ride's almost here, you gotta be ready."

I slid into a chair and started shoveling food in.

"Why the hell is she going there?" Ronnie muttered, hauling Blair off the floor.

"She wanted some quality time with her dad before college starts. Why would I stop her?" Mom smiled at me, and I beamed back. Honestly, I had no clue how this trip would hide the mate bond from Damon, but I didn't care. I just needed out. Fast.

"Yeah, Dad rang me up this morning," I said, throwing Ronnie a sugary-sweet look. "Haven't seen him since Christmas, and since he offered to buy the ticket, I begged Mom." 

Blair actually smiled at that. "Wait, you're actually leaving?" 

"Oh, yeah. Gone all summer." I smirked right at her. "But don't get any ideas. My door is locked, and it's staying locked." My face went dead serious. I locked eyes with her and pushed my Alpha command straight into her skull.

"Lyra!" Ronnie barked. "No Alpha commands on your stepsister! You know the rules!"

"I wouldn't have to use it, Ronnie, if she hadn't been sneaking around my closet this morning trying to steal my clothes." I turned my gaze to her, raising an eyebrow. *Go ahead. Try me. Lie.*

"Is that true, Blair?" Ronnie looked down at her. 

I kept my eyes locked on her face. She opened her mouth to spin some BS. 

"Don't even try to lie," I warned. "I'll just force the truth out of you anyway."

Blair threw a massive tantrum, stomping her foot and screeching. "Fine! Yes!" she yelled. "Happy now? I went in there to grab her clothes because I know she's Damon's mate!"

I threw my hands up, acting totally clueless. "Uh, what? How could you possibly know that? We haven't even done the scent thing yet!"

"Because he smelled you on me, duh!" Her voice went so high it practically shattered glass. My ears literally throbbed.

"Okay, pipe down. You're giving us all a headache. Just explain," Mom said, sitting next to me and rubbing her temples.

Blair pouted, crossing her arms. "Last month, when Damon turned eighteen, I wore Lyra's dress. He sniffed me and said I smelled amazing. But the second I'm not wearing her stuff? He doesn't even look at me."

"So he likes my scent. Big deal. Doesn't make us mates," I scoffed, completely shutting down the idea. No way in hell. If I rejected him, the bond was dead anyway, and there was zero chance I'd ever accept him. That was a promise. Damon was the absolute last guy on earth I'd ever let touch me.

"Stop playing dumb, Lyra! We all know what a wolf liking your scent means!" Blair burst into tears, hiding her face in her hands. "He's the one I want, Daddy! I won't take anyone else! But he wants *her*!" She pointed a shaking finger at me.

I rolled my eyes. "Please. I don't want your sloppy seconds, Blair. Even if he *were* my mate—which I'm not saying he is—hell would freeze over before I ever accepted him. Honestly, I'd rather take the Lycan King over Damon any day."

Blair gasped, and I just threw my head back and laughed. 

The Lycan King was basically our world's boogeyman. The last living Lycan, hiding out in the wild. Supposedly, only the high council ever saw his face. But hey, I wasn't joking. I'd take a monster over Damon in a heartbeat.

"You're full of it," Blair snapped. "He's the Alpha!"

"So?"

"Everyone wants to be Luna!"

"Yeah, only idiots want that job." I turned back to my plate and finished my breakfast while Ronnie tried to quiet her down. 

A car horn honked outside, and Mom stood up. "That's your ride."

I nodded, stood up, gave Mom a quick goodbye kiss, and walked out the door.

###chapter 4
I shoved my bags in the trunk, dove into the backseat, and clicked the belt. Before my lungs could even take in air, I scrambled over the console and threw myself right into the driver’s arms.

He let out a low chuckle, making my eyes sting. "Hey there, kiddo."

"Uncle Finnian! God, I missed you." I hauled myself over the seat and dropped into the shotgun spot. "What the hell are you doing here anyway?" Finnian was my dad’s beta. Not blood, but he basically raised me.

"You seriously think I’d let my favorite smartass niece head to pack territory solo? Hell no."

"Dad sent you, didn't he?" I snorted.

"Yep, your old man sent me. Dude is a total worrywart." He grinned, chuckling along with me. "The second your mom called, he prepped the private jet."

"He didn't need to do all that." I rolled my eyes, clicking my seatbelt into place.

"Of course he did. He barely gets to see you, and now you're dumping your whole summer on us. What gives?" My uncle shot me a look. I just shook my head.

"I don't even want to be here."

"Why's that?"

I stared down at my hands, fingers twisting into knots. "I'm terrified my fated mate is lurking around here. And I really don't want to be right. I figured if I ran, I could buy myself some time."

"Why the hell wouldn't you want your mate?" my uncle asked, gunning the engine down the highway toward the runway.

"I'll lay it all out for you and Dad. Just... not right now." My uncle studied my face, searching for clues, before finally nodding.

"Fine. But I want the whole damn story."

"You'll get it, promise." I pointed at the windshield. "Now watch the road before you kill us both!" I lunged, grabbing the steering wheel to yank us back into our lane.

"Holy shit!" Uncle Finnian ripped the wheel back, eyes locked on the asphalt. "I'm just stressed about you, kid." I couldn't help but laugh. Werewolves stop aging at twenty-five, so he looked about my age.

"I know, I know." I slumped back into my seat with a sigh. "Trust me, what happened isn't going to make you feel any better." I wiped my face. "I don't even get why Mom shipped me off to Dad. She just said he could fix things."

"Well, let's get back fast so we can sort this mess out, Sugar." My uncle slammed the gas, and we tore into the airport in seconds.

We tossed my bags inside and boarded the jet, getting comfortable. "Close your eyes. You look like absolute hell, and we've got a few hours." My uncle gave my head a quick pat, sat across from me, and flipped open his laptop.

"Work?"

"Always." He nodded.

"Hey, can you teach me some business stuff this summer?" A plan was clicking into place. A way to stay free from my pathetic excuse of a mate, and make a boatload of cash while doing it.

"Sure thing, Sugar." My uncle flashed a grin. "You know, your dad would teach you everything he knows if you just let him."

"I actually asked to transfer to your pack permanently." I snuggled into the blanket the flight attendant handed me. Finnian froze solid.

"What the hell is going on?" His eyes flared.

"I'll explain later. Just promise you'll believe me and won't judge."

"Always, Sugar." He smiled, turning back to his screen. "Now get some sleep."

"On it." I rolled over and passed out instantly.

A shake on my shoulder woke me up. Finnian was hovering. "We're here."

I let out a massive yawn, popped my jaw, and rubbed my eyes. "Got it." I handed back the blanket and wiped my face again. "Thanks."

"Anytime, Princess." The flight attendant smiled. I realized a second too late that she was one of our pack members, too.

"You don't have to call me Princess."

"You're the Alpha's kid." She gave a quick bow and left us to it.

"Move it, your dad has already mind-linked me three times since we touched down." Finnian laughed, ushering me toward the waiting SUV. Thirty minutes later, we crossed into pack territory. "Your dad would let you move here in a heartbeat if you wanted, Sugar."

"I know. But Alpha Dan won't let me leave..." I sighed, looking out the window. "I think he suspects I'm running from something, and he won't let me go until he gets the truth."

"You gonna spill yet, Sugar?"

I hesitated as we pulled up to the massive pack house. Before I could even speak, the car door flew open. Strong arms wrapped around me, and a scent washed over me that instantly quieted my racing heart.

"Dad."

"Hey, my girl." His deep voice instantly grounded me, and my eyes started to burn.

"I missed you so much." I sniffled as he unbuckled my seatbelt and pulled me out.

"Missed you too, kiddo." He kissed my temple. "Now, we need to talk." He bolted inside with me in his arms before I could say a word, Finnian sprinting to keep up.

"Slow down, you idiot! Some of us aren't that fast!" Finnian panted, struggling behind us. My laughter echoed through the pack house hallways. We finally crashed in my dad's office. Finnian was out of breath and scowling. God, I missed these guys.

"Tell me what's wrong, kid." I looked around, my tongue tying itself in knots. Dad cupped my face, shaking his head. "Nothing you say changes a thing. I believe you, no matter how wild it sounds."

"Same here, Sugar."

My chest loosened seeing how dead-serious they were. They'd believe my crazy story. No matter how insane it sounded, my dad and Finnian had my back.

I didn't have to worry about looking crazy here.

So, I finally took a breath and let it all out.

###chapter 5
"I already lived once. And I died." 

The words stumbled out of my mouth. My dad went stiff as a board. I shot a look at Finnian, and he instantly bolted the door, waving his hands to cast a silence spell. The air in the room went dead quiet, but my eyes were locked on my dad. 

"This morning, I woke up six years in the past. Before this, I lived to twenty-four. I had a baby. And my mate? He ripped my pup right out of my stomach."

A double growl shook the damn walls. Dad and Finnian looked ready to kill. 

I threw my hands up. "Stop! Listen. He dumped me for my stepsister. She fed him lies about me cheating, said the kid wasn't his. So he butchered us both. Used silver scalpels. That killed any love I had left for him." I stared up at my dad, tears finally spilling over.

"Baby girl..." Dad choked out.

I cut him off with a raised hand. "I’m not mating with him, Dad. No way. I won't survive it. I have to rewrite this whole damn thing. First step? Hiding my scent. I told Mom what I needed, and she dialed you. So, what's the plan? How do we fix this?" Panic started clawing at my throat. "I can't die again. I can't let him tear my baby out of me just to realize it was his own blood. I won't bring a life into this world just to watch it get slaughtered, Dad. I just can't." My chest felt like it was splitting open. I wanted payback, sure, but right now? I was just finally mourning my dead baby.

"Oh, sweetheart," Finnian whispered. 

Then, my dad snapped. 

"Who?" 

The word came straight from the deepest pit of hell. *Crack!* His fist slammed the desk, splintering the thick wood. I looked up. It wasn't my dad anymore. It was Obsidian, his wolf, staring back at me. 

"Who touched you, my pup? Who killed my grandpup?" Obsidian’s voice was a terrifying, low rumble. His eyes promised pure murder.

"Damon. The Alpha's son," I whispered. 

The final puzzle piece clicked. The heavy silence broke, and my dad’s wolf took over, shifting into a massive black beast. I shrieked. Finnian lunged, throwing his body right in front of the door.

Obsidian bared his fangs, but Finnian didn't budge. "You can't go kill him for something he hasn't even done yet, Obsidian! Get a grip! You know the rules. You went through this exact same shit!" 

The black wolf just snarled.

"Dad, please!" I begged. If he walked out that door, Damon and Blair were dead meat, and the Council would hunt him down. 

Obsidian whipped around. Seeing my wrecked face, his anger melted. He trotted over, licked the tears off my cheeks, then retreated behind the desk to shift back into human form.

"My bad, Lyra. Lost my head for a second." He grabbed some shorts from a drawer and pulled them on. He wiped his face, then sat back down. "Well. Guess it's time to spill our own secrets."

"Dad?" I sniffled, looking up.

"Look, I'm not just a regular werewolf. Obviously, Obsidian is a huge part of me," he said with a weak chuckle. I managed a small smile. "But my mom? She was a shaman. A witch. My dad had to have her, even if it was just a one-night stand. And boom—here I am."

"A witch?" My hands dropped. 

He gave me a sad, tight smile. "Yeah. You would've loved her. But witches don't get our lifespan. They age like humans. Gone in a blink. She passed way before I met your mother." He shook his head. "But she had a gift. Exactly what you just described—a do-over. The Moon Goddess passed that magic down to us. I got my second chance when I was your age, too."

I jumped back, eyes wide. "Wait, what?"

He nodded. "I never actually cheated on your mom," he said softly. "I used an Alpha command on a female wolf to make her lie about us sleeping together. See, in my first life, I stayed with your mom. We had three beautiful pups. But one night, enemies raided us. They slaughtered all four of you." He swallowed hard, his throat tight.

"Dad..."

"I couldn't watch you die again. Not my babies. So when I woke up four years in the past, I made my move. You were just a tiny baby. I never got your brothers or sister back, and that absolutely destroyed me for a while. But I had you." He choked back tears. I rushed to his side. "So I told your mom I cheated."

"She said she felt the bond break," I murmured.

He nodded slowly. "When a wolf betrays their fated mate, the pain is pure agony."

"Yeah, it damn well is," Finnian growled from the door. 

I whipped my head toward him. Suddenly, it clicked. "Wait. Mom and Ronnie..."

"It doesn't happen enough to be a habit," my dad growled.

"But it happens enough that you still feel the burn," Finnian shot back.

"Mom has no idea," I said, wrapping my arms around my dad. "She'd lose her mind if she knew the truth."

"I know, princess. That's why you can't say a word. I cheated death, so I beat my fate... but finding out the truth now? It would absolutely destroy her." My dad squeezed me tight.

"So she actually felt you with another woman?" I hugged him back. 

He shook his head. "No. I used my magic to mimic the pain of a broken bond. She was sobbing in our bedroom, and I was in the hallway, breaking my own heart."

"Oh, Dad..."

"It was either lose her and you, or lose everything. And I knew this way, I'd still get to watch my little girl grow up." My dad pulled back, wiping his eyes. "Anyway, I'm not telling you this to make you feel sorry for me. I'm telling you because you have that same magic. You can hide your scent, easily. And this summer, I'm going to teach you how to weaponize it."

Finnian grunted, "Yeah, okay. I was dead wrong."

I gave him a firm nod. "Alright. Let's sort out the rest of these guys first. I'll figure out how this oath magic works, and we'll do it later." I stood up and threw my hand out to help him up. "Deal?"
